# 2012 Stockport Metropolitan Borough Council Election

The 2012 Stockport Metropolitan Borough Council election took place on **3 May 2012** as part of the local elections held across England that year.

## Key Details

**Elections held for:** One-third of the council seats (21 out of 63 seats)

**Context:** This was part of the regular electoral cycle where Stockport holds elections by thirds in three out of every four years.

## Results

The **Liberal Democrats** maintained overall control of the council, though the results reflected the challenging national political climate for the party during the Conservative-Liberal Democrat coalition government period.

**General outcome:**
- The Liberal Democrats retained their majority on the council
- Labour made gains, reflecting their stronger position nationally at this time
- The Conservatives faced difficulties
- UKIP was beginning to show increased support in some areas

## Political Context

This election occurred:
- During the Conservative-Liberal Democrat coalition government (2010-2015)
- At a time when the Liberal Democrats were facing significant backlash nationally over tuition fees and coalition policies
- When Labour was recovering from their 2010 general election defeat under Ed Miliband's leadership

Stockport had been a Liberal Democrat stronghold for many years, and they managed to maintain control despite national headwinds.
